newsitem.title: USA: Ore. 474 MW gas-fired unit displaced by hydropower.
newsitem.headline: Ore. 474 MW gas-fired unit displaced by hydropower.

text.p: The 474 megawatt (MW) natural gas-fired Hermiston generating plant in Oregon will shut Saturday until July, displaced by lower-cost hydropower supplies, sources familiar with the plant said Friday.
"It's not so much that gas prices are high as it is that hydro is super-cheap," said a source at the plant.
Industry sources said Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) agreed to supply PacifiCorp, Hermiston's operator, with hydropower at a cost below that of running the plant.
BPA said earlier this week it is seeking to arrange similar contracts with thermal generation plants throughout Northwest.
